### 1B — Nuclear responsibility

- `IND-2023-1B-004`: India’s declared doctrine remains no-first-use and retaliation-only. Precise locator: Nuclear Transparency, India doctrine page, doctrine section. Attribution: formal national doctrine; not proof of Modi authorship. [Source](https://nucleartransparency.org/country/india/)
- `IND-2023-1B-005`: India’s 2023 nuclear capability included an operational deterrent estimated at roughly 164 warheads. Locator: SIPRI Yearbook 2023, “World nuclear forces,” January 2023 table. Attribution: state capability, persistent through 2023. [Source](https://www.sipri.org/yearbook/2023/07)
- `IND-2023-1B-006`: India conducted a January 2023 Prithvi-II training launch, explicitly describing the missile as part of nuclear deterrence. Locator: PIB release, 10 January 2023. Attribution: government/defense establishment; Modi-period executive responsibility is authority-based. [Source](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1890129)
- `IND-2023-1B-007`: India’s doctrine contains a significant exception for retaliation after chemical or biological attack. Locator: Arms Control Association doctrine summary. Contrary evidence to a simple restraint interpretation. [Source](https://www.armscontrol.org/act/2019-10/news-briefs/india-considers-no-first-use-changes)

Shortfall: no located 2023 Modi statement changing doctrine, ordering nuclear deployment, or making a nuclear threat. The 2024 CDS statement is post-period and should remain contextual only. [Source](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2028825)

### 2B — International peace and aggression

- `IND-2023-2B-005`: Modi and Xi agreed in August 2023 to intensify efforts toward border de-escalation. Locator: AP report, 24 August 2023, foreign-secretary briefing. Direct Modi attribution. [Source](https://apnews.com/article/8491c234c15ab3457f2fc60fcac6ab66)
- `IND-2023-2B-006`: The agreement concerned a continuing Ladakh standoff involving tens of thousands of troops. Locator: same AP report, opening paragraphs. Persistent conflict context, not a new 2023 war. [Source](https://apnews.com/article/8491c234c15ab3457f2fc60fcac6ab66)
- `IND-2023-2B-007`: India’s 2023–24 defense allocation rose 13% to ₹5.94 lakh crore. Locator: PIB budget release. Attribution: national executive budget policy; spending alone does not establish aggression. [Source](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1895472)
- `IND-2023-2B-008`: SIPRI estimated India’s 2023 military expenditure at $83.6 billion, fourth globally. Locator: SIPRI 2023 military-expenditure fact sheet. [Source](https://www.sipri.org/sites/default/files/2024-04/2404_fs_milex_2023.pdf)
- `IND-2023-2B-009`: UN-linked reporting identified 22 India-based suppliers connected to arms transfers to Myanmar’s military. Locator: UN Special Rapporteur infographic, 17 May 2023. Attribution is supplier/state-policy level, not a Modi order. [Source](https://www.ohchr.org/sites/default/files/documents/countries/myanmar/infographic-sr-myanmar-2023-05-17.pdf)

Contrary: India’s stated border policy emphasized negotiated disengagement, while China disputed the extent of any August agreement. [Source](https://indianexpress.com/article/india/gap-between-delhi-beijing-xi-jinping-meeting-lac-disengagement-8909852/)

### 3B — Domestic safety and violence

- `IND-2023-3B-005`: Manipur violence caused more than 100 deaths and tens of thousands of displacements by July 2023. Locator: HRW, 21 July 2023. [Source](https://www.hrw.org/news/2023/07/21/indian-government-finally-responds-violence-manipur)
- `IND-2023-3B-006`: Internet restrictions continued during the violence and were criticized as harmful to credible information and law enforcement. Locator: same HRW report. [Source](https://www.hrw.org/news/2023/07/21/indian-government-finally-responds-violence-manipur)
- `IND-2023-3B-007`: The Modi-led central government established a formal Commission of Inquiry on 4 June 2023. Locator: PIB/MHA release, lines 9–12. Direct authority-based attribution and contrary evidence to a claim of complete non-response. [Source](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1929742)
- `IND-2023-3B-008`: Modi stated in his 10 August parliamentary speech that the central and state governments were pursuing punishment and restoration of peace. Locator: PM speech, lines 329–330. This is a ruler statement, not independent confirmation of effectiveness. [Source](https://www.pmindia.gov.in/en/news_updates/pms-reply-to-the-no-confidence-motion-in-lok-sabha-on-10th-august-2023/)
- `IND-2023-3B-009`: The U.S. State Department recorded conflict abuses, unlawful killings, arbitrary detention, and restrictions on expression during 2023. Locator: India 2023 Human Rights Report, opening summary. [Source](https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2107729.html)

Shortfall: evidence still does not establish that Modi personally ordered abuses. Responsibility remains distributed among central authorities, the Manipur government, police, armed groups, and local political actors.

### 4B — Political freedom

- `IND-2023-4B-006`: Freedom House described India as having elected institutions and a formally independent judiciary while also documenting attacks on press freedom under the Modi government. Locator: India 2023 country report, political-process and media sections. [Source](https://freedomhouse.org/country/india/freedom-world/2023)
- `IND-2023-4B-007`: The government blocked the BBC documentary concerning Modi’s Gujarat record and restricted circulation of clips. Locator: AP, 25 January 2023. Direct executive attribution. [Source](https://apnews.com/article/34b8e834736ab6b9e36eff4f99704145)
- `IND-2023-4B-008`: Delhi police raided NewsClick journalists and used UAPA-related proceedings in October 2023. Locator: TIME report, 4 October 2023. Attribution: central law-enforcement action; personal Modi direction not established. [Source](https://time.com/6320395/india-newsclick-raid-press-freedom/)
- `IND-2023-4B-009`: HRW documented that the government ordered removal of a Manipur violence video while the Supreme Court demanded action. Locator: HRW, 21 July 2023. [Source](https://www.hrw.org/news/2023/07/21/indian-government-finally-responds-violence-manipur)
- `IND-2023-4B-010`: The Supreme Court remained an institutional check, including intervention in Manipur-related proceedings. Locator: Supreme Court order, 15 December 2023. [Source](https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2023/19206/19206_2023_1_28_49089_Order_15-Dec-2023.pdf)

Contrary: elections, parliament, opposition parties, and judicial review continued functioning. These facts limit any categorical claim that political competition ceased.

### 5B — Economic prosperity

- `IND-2023-5B-005`: IMF directors described India’s 2023 performance as strong, resilient, and financially stable under prudent macroeconomic policies. Locator: Article IV consultation, paragraph beginning “Executive Directors.” [Source](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2023/12/18/pr23458-india-imf-exec-board-concludes-2023-art-iv-consult)
- `IND-2023-5B-006`: The same IMF assessment identified labor-market reforms as necessary to raise employment and growth. Locator: Article IV consultation, labor-market reform discussion. [Source](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2023/12/18/pr23458-india-imf-exec-board-concludes-2023-art-iv-consult)
- `IND-2023-5B-007`: Official PLFS data reported female labor-force participation rising to 37% in 2022–23, with unemployment also declining. Locator: PIB summary, lines 37–42 and 391–392. [Source](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1966154)
- `IND-2023-5B-008`: IMF research identified continuing poverty, inequality, consumption, and employment concerns after the pandemic. Locator: 2023 working paper abstract and methodology. [Source](https://www.imf.org/en/publications/wp/issues/2023/07/20/inequality-and-poverty-in-india-impact-of-covid-19-pandemic-and-policy-response-535908)
- `IND-2023-5B-009`: World Bank country material identifies persistent informality, low female participation, unequal access to quality services, and regional disparities despite poverty reduction. Locator: India country overview. [Source](https://www.worldbank.org/ext/en/country/india)

Shortfall: direct causal attribution from these macro outcomes to Modi’s individual 2023 decisions remains limited.

### 6B — Welfare and human development

- `IND-2023-6B-005`: India and the World Bank signed two $500 million health-sector loans in March 2023 for infrastructure and pandemic preparedness. Locator: World Bank release, 3 March 2023. [Source](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2023/03/03/world-bank-signs-a-1-billion-program-to-support-india-s-health-sector-for-pandemic-preparedness-and-enhanced-health-serv)
- `IND-2023-6B-006`: UNICEF’s 2023 India reporting covered health, nutrition, education, and child protection programs implemented with Indian ministries. Locator: UNICEF India Annual Report 2023. [Source](https://www.unicef.org/media/152691/file/India-2023)
- `IND-2023-6B-007`: UNICEF continued to identify malnutrition and learning poverty as major constraints despite selected improvements. Locator: UNICEF nutrition and education pages. [Source](https://www.unicef.org/india/reports/indias-progress-malnutrition-and-non-communicable-diseases-insights-nfhs)
- `IND-2023-6B-008`: Official Indian reporting claimed improved child-nutrition indicators and continued Mission Poshan 2.0 implementation. Locator: PIB nutrition release, December 2023. Self-reported government evidence. [Source](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=1988614)
- `IND-2023-6B-009`: PLFS data provide a contemporaneous welfare-adjacent outcome indicator: female labor-force participation reached 37% in 2022–23, while female unemployment fell to 2.9% under the stated measure. Locator: PIB PLFS tables. [Source](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1966154)

Shortfall: independent 2023 outcome evidence remains weaker than program and institutional reporting; regional distribution and implementation failures need further work.

### 7B — Integrity and corruption

- `IND-2023-7B-005`: The Supreme Court’s electoral-bonds judgment records that the scheme operated through February 2024 and required disclosure of donor, amount, recipient, and credit-date information. Locator: judgment, paragraphs 217–218 and related interim-order passages. Post-period adjudication of a scheme operating during 2023. [Source](https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2017/27935/27935_2017_1_1501_50573_Judgement_15-Feb-2024.pdf)
- `IND-2023-7B-006`: The Court later held the electoral-bonds framework unconstitutional and violative of Article 19(1)(a). Locator: judgment and summary of operative holding. This is later legal assessment, not a 2023 event. [Source](https://indianexpress.com/article/india/supreme-court-electoral-bonds-9162593/)
- `IND-2023-7B-007`: A 2023 petition by opposition parties alleged misuse of the Enforcement Directorate and CBI against political rivals; the Supreme Court rejected the broad petition without endorsing the allegations. Locator: AP/NDTV coverage of the April 2023 proceedings. [Source](https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/setback-for-opposition-in-supreme-court-over-misuse-of-central-agencies-3922536)
- `IND-2023-7B-008`: The Enforcement Directorate publicly claimed that politicians comprised less than 3% of its cases and defended its conviction record. Locator: Indian Express report, March 2023. Direct contrary institutional response. [Source](https://indianexpress.com/article/india/under-fire-ed-says-high-conviction-rate-politicians-are-accused-in-3-cases-8499772/)
- `IND-2023-7B-009`: An Indian Express investigation reported that many politicians under probe received relief after joining the BJP, while agencies disputed the interpretation. Locator: investigation published 2024, used only as retrospective evidence about the 2023-related pattern. [Source](https://indianexpress.com/article/express-exclusive/since-2014-25-opposition-leaders-facing-corruption-probe-crossed-over-to-bjp-23-of-them-got-reprieve-9247737/)

Shortfall: no defensible evidence of Modi’s personal enrichment, personal receipt of corrupt benefits, or a documented personal order.

### 8B — Governance effectiveness

- `IND-2023-8B-006`: Chandrayaan-3 achieved a lunar soft landing on 23 August 2023. Locator: ISRO mission page. Attribution: national executive sponsorship with substantial institutional/technical autonomy. [Source](https://www.isro.gov.in/Chandrayaan3.html)
- `IND-2023-8B-007`: The Indian government publicly presented Chandrayaan-3 as a major 2023 national achievement under Modi-era governance. Locator: PIB, 22 December 2023, lines 20–22 and 64–69. Government self-description. [Source](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1989635)
- `IND-2023-8B-008`: India’s G20 presidency produced a consensus New Delhi Leaders’ Declaration and supported African Union membership. Locator: AP G20 report, September 2023. [Source](https://apnews.com/article/india-g20-modi-1e26d74e0dcbfad4eebaf6f1b7df404f432)
- `IND-2023-8B-009`: External observers characterized the G20 outcome as diplomatically successful but noted softer Ukraine language and lack of direct condemnation of Russia. Locator: HRW World Report 2024, India chapter. [Source](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/india)
- `IND-2023-8B-010`: Modi’s August 2023 no-confidence speech demonstrates direct executive engagement with the Manipur crisis, while also deflecting responsibility toward earlier governments. Locator: PM speech, lines 329 and 377. [Source](https://www.pmindia.gov.in/en/news_updates/pms-reply-to-the-no-confidence-motion-in-lok-sabha-on-10th-august-2023/)
- `IND-2023-8B-011`: The Manipur crisis prompted a no-confidence motion and sustained criticism of executive capacity. Locator: Time, July 2023. [Source](https://time.com/6297996/modi-no-confidence-vote-manipur/)
